Advances: specled.spec_review

Follow-up from critical-review F1 (Medium, test gap) on specled_-3q1 (merged as 0.3.3, PR #8). The must requirement specled.spec_review.gh_pages_privilege_separation is backed only by a workflow_file verification, which in SpecLedEx asserts only that the target file exists and contains the cover-id string (lib/specled_ex/verifier.ex: existence check ~L706, String.contains? cover-id ~L779). It asserts nothing about the YAML job structure, so mix spec.check stays green even if a future edit re-merges the render/deploy jobs, promotes top-level permissions to write, or drops the deploy ref pin. The invariant holds today; only its guard is weak. Proposed fix: add a command-tier verification that parses priv/spec_init/workflows/spec_review.yml.eex and asserts the two-job split (render has no write scope; deploy holds the write scopes, needs render, runs no PR code; top-level permissions read-only).

VERDICT: still_applicable   EFFORT: small
Mandate confirmed still applicable as written; no narrowing needed.

== SCOPED REMAINING WORK ==
All of it. Two edits:

(A) New test file — suggested path test/specled_ex/spec_review_workflow_test.exs (async: true). Read priv/spec_init/workflows/spec_review.yml.eex and parse it with `YamlElixir.read_from_string!/1` (yaml_elixir ~> 2.11 is an unconditional dep, mix.exs:133). The template contains ZERO EEx tags (`grep -c "<%"` = 0), so it parses as plain YAML with no rendering step. Assert the four clauses of the must statement at .spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md:221-232:
  1. top-level read-only default: `workflow["permissions"] == %{"contents" => "read"}` — no key whose value is "write".
  2. two-job split: `Map.keys(workflow["jobs"]) |> Enum.sort() == ["deploy", "render"]` and `deploy["needs"]` includes "render".
  3. render holds no write scope: every value in `render["permissions"]` is in ~w(read none) — specifically refute `"pull-requests" => "write"` and `"contents" => "write"`.
  4. deploy holds the write scopes AND runs no PR code: `deploy["permissions"] == %{"contents" => "write", "pull-requests" => "write"}`; every `actions/checkout` step in deploy pins `with.ref` to a base-ref expression (assert it equals "${{ github.base_ref }}", i.e. refute an unpinned checkout and refute any `github.event.pull_request.head` ref); and no deploy step's `run` invokes `mix ` (the PR-code execution surface) — assert `mix ` appears only in render steps.
Falsify each assertion before committing (mutate the template in a scratch copy: merge the jobs, promote top-level permissions to write, drop `needs`, drop the deploy `ref` pin) and confirm the test goes RED for each.
Gotcha for the implementer: yaml_elixir/yamerl is YAML 1.1, so the `on:` key parses as the boolean `true`, not the string "on" (confirmed: top-level keys come back as ['name', True, 'permissions', 'concurrency', 'jobs']). Do not key off `"on"`; if trigger assertions are wanted, look up `true`.

(B) Spec edit — .spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md, `spec-verification` block. Append (or insert alongside the other `kind: command` entries, :831-908):
```
- kind: command
  target: mix test test/specled_ex/spec_review_workflow_test.exs
  execute: true
  covers:
    - specled.spec_review.gh_pages_privilege_separation
```
Keep the existing `workflow_file` entry at :958-963 as-is — it still carries `specled.spec_review.gh_pages_distribution`, which has no other backing.

Optional, not required by any gate (checked: no "must requirement without scenario" detector exists in lib/): a `spec-scenarios` block covering the id.

BLOCKER 1 - deploy can check out PR code via `run:` and the suite stays green.
test/specled_ex/spec_review_workflow_test.exs:84-86 filters checkout steps by `step["uses"] |> String.starts_with?("actions/checkout")`. A deploy step that hand-rolls the checkout has no `uses` key at all, so it is never inspected. Verified mutation (all 4 tests green):

        git checkout prhead
        bash ./scripts/postprocess.sh

That is a direct violation of the requirement's own words - "the write-scoped job shall not check out or execute pull-request-provided code" - inside the job holding `contents: write` + `pull-requests: write`, which already runs raw `git`. The `uses`-only filter is the wrong shape for this clause.
A correct version additionally scans every deploy `run:` string and rejects PR-ref acquisition, e.g. `refute Regex.match?(~r{pull/\S*/(head|merge)}, run)` and `refute String.contains?(run, @pr_head_ref_fragment)`, and allowlists deploy's `uses:` set (only `actions/checkout`, `actions/download-artifact`) so a new action cannot smuggle a checkout in either.

BLOCKER 2 - `invokes_mix?/1` (line 122) evades on 5 of 9 ordinary CI forms.
The regex `~r/(^|\n)[ \t]*mix[ \t]/` is anchored to line start. Measured:

    CAUGHT  mix deps.get
    CAUGHT  mix\tdeps.get
    EVADES  MIX_ENV=prod mix run script.exs
    EVADES  cd apps/x && mix release
    EVADES  ./bin/mix spec.review
    EVADES  OUT=$(mix spec.review --output x.html)
    EVADES  bash -c 'mix spec.review'
    EVADES  elixir -S mix spec.review

Verified mutation: appending `MIX_ENV=prod mix run ./rendered/hook.exs` to deploy's gh-pages step leaves all 4 tests green - and `rendered/` is the artifact produced from PR head, so that is PR-influenced code executing in the write-scoped job. The line-anchor exists to avoid the backticked `` `mix spec.review` `` in deploy's comment body (template line 184); stripping backtick spans first solves that without the anchor. I ran this replacement 12/12 correct on the table above and green against the real template (render 3 hits, deploy 0), so it is drop-in with no template change:

    defp invokes_mix?(run) when is_binary(run) do
      run
      |> String.replace(~r/`[^`]*`/, "")
      |> then(&Regex.match?(~r{(?<![\w.-])[\w./-]*mix[ \t]}, &1))
    end

Neither predicate inspects `uses:` steps or a job-level `uses:` reusable-workflow call; worth a comment noting that limit even after the fix.

WARNING - "render holds no write scope" (line 59) passes when `render.permissions` is absent entirely.
Line 61's `render["permissions"] || %{}` makes the comprehension and both refutes vacuous. Verified: deleting render's `permissions:` block leaves this test green. It does not violate the requirement today only because line 33 pins top-level to exactly `%{"contents" => "read"}`, so render would inherit read-only - i.e. the clause is covered by a different test, not this one. The asymmetry is unjustified given deploy is asserted by exact map equality at line 79. Assert the same way: `assert render["permissions"] == %{"contents" => "read"}`. Related: `permissions: write-all` (the real GH shorthand for full write) parses as a binary and raises `Protocol.UndefinedError` from the comprehension rather than asserting - still red, but the failure is unreadable.

WARNING - dead assertions that can never fire.
Lines 35-41 run a write-scope scan on a map already pinned by `==` at line 33; lines 99-102 refute nil/PR-head on a `ref` already pinned by `==` at line 96. Both are unreachable. They read as independent coverage and are not, which is exactly the wrong signal in a security guard.

RECOMMENDATION - split the line 72 test.
It asserts deploy permissions, checkout pinning, mix absence, and a render canary in one test. For the load-bearing security assertion, a failure should name its clause without reading the message body.

RECOMMENDATION - cwd-dependence.
`@workflow_path` (line 14) is repo-relative. Fine under `mix test` from root, which is how the verification target runs, but `Path.expand("../../priv/spec_init/workflows/spec_review.yml.eex", __DIR__)` removes the assumption for free.

What holds up (checked, not assumed):

- (a) is a non-issue in this stack: I verified yamerl keeps `on` as the string `"on"` (`Map.keys/1` returns `["concurrency", "jobs", "name", "on", "permissions"]`, `wf[true]` is nil) - unlike YAML 1.1 loaders in other languages. The test never keys off it anyway.
- (c) first half is right: line 92 iterates EVERY `actions/checkout` step, not just the first, and line 96's exact equality against `${{ github.base_ref }}` is strictly stronger than "not PR head" - it rejects unpinned, PR-head, and any other wrong ref in one assertion. Mutating the ref to `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` fails correctly.
- Line 49's exact job-key pin catches a smuggled third job: adding a `notify` job with `contents: write` fails correctly.
- Line 68/69 equivalent - granting render `pull-requests: write` fails correctly.
- Line 114's `render_mix_steps != []` canary is the best thing in the file: it makes the deploy mix-absence assertion non-vacuous at the detector level. It is why BLOCKER 2 is a hole in the pattern rather than a silently broken detector. Keep it after the fix.
- (f)/(g) clean: pure `File.read!` + `YamlElixir.read_from_string!`, no shelling out, no processes, no tmp, no `Process.sleep`, `async: true`. 4 tests in 0.03s - cheap enough for bare `mix spec.check` preflight. `setup_all` is the right scope for the immutable parsed doc shared by 4 tests.
- `.spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md` verification entry is `kind: command` / `execute: true` / covers the one subject; tag forms match repo convention (both list-moduletag and scalar `@tag spec:` are in use elsewhere).

No files edited; full suite not run.

Reasoning: The critic is right on both blockers and neither is an over-reach. The
operative clause of specled.spec_review.gh_pages_privilege_separation
(.spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md:221-232) reads, verbatim: "The workflow's top-level
permissions shall default to read-only, and **the write-scoped job shall not check out
or execute pull-request-provided code**" — with the preceding clause "so that no single
job both runs pull-request-provided code and holds a write-scoped token." The
requirement quantifies over the ACT of checking out and the ACT of executing, not over
the `uses: actions/checkout` syntax. test/specled_ex/spec_review_workflow_test.exs:84-86
filters candidate steps by `is_binary(step["uses"]) and String.starts_with?(step["uses"],
"actions/checkout")`, so a `run:`-tier checkout is never inspected — and that is not a
contrived shape here: deploy's own steps at template :139-171 already run raw `git
fetch` / `git worktree add` in a `run:` block, so a hand-rolled `git fetch
origin pull/N/head:prhead && git checkout prhead` is the same tooling the job already
uses. The `invokes_mix?/1` line-anchor at :122 has the same defect on the "or execute"
half. This ticket exists precisely to retire a weak proxy (workflow_file = existence +
cover-id substring); shipping a `uses:`-shaped proxy in its place reproduces the original
finding at a new tier.

Mechanical scope is clean and NOT the reason for the bounce: `git diff --name-only
2023373d..HEAD` = exactly 2 files (.spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md +5,
test/specled_ex/spec_review_workflow_test.exs new); the template, mix.exs, mix.lock,
.spec/realization_hashes.json, CHANGELOG.md and VERSION are all absent from the diff
(filtered `git diff --name-only` over those paths returns 0 lines). Requirement text
:221-232 byte-unchanged; the workflow_file entry survives at :963-967 still carrying
gh_pages_distribution. Wiring trace on the one disclosed seam: the new `kind: command`
entry at :916 targets `mix test test/specled_ex/spec_review_workflow_test.exs`, that
path exists in the tree, and the entry sits inside the spec-verification block (closing
fence :968) — no disconnected production path, so no INTEGRATION_REGRESSION_LATENT.
Intent-wise it IS a command-tier guard (File.read! + YamlElixir parse of real job/
permission structure), not a substring check — the defect is the guard's aperture, not
its tier.

On the critic's line-anchor rationale: confirmed correct against the template. The only
`mix` token in the deploy job is the backticked `` `mix spec.review` `` inside the
printf body at :184, mid-line, so an unanchored naive `mix[ \t]` would go RED against
the UNMUTATED template — that is exactly why the anchor is there. Stripping backtick
spans first removes that collision with no other false positive in this file: deploy has
no remaining `mix` substring anywhere, and render keeps its 3 real invocations
(:83 `mix deps.get`, :96 `mix spec.cover.test`, :100 `mix spec.review`), so the :113
non-vacuity canary stays satisfied. Two judgement points before pasting it: the
backtick-strip is whole-string, so an ODD number of backticks anywhere in a run block
would pair a comment backtick with a distant one and silently swallow real commands
between them (fail-OPEN in a security detector — strip per line, or assert balance); and
`[\w./-]*mix[ \t]` will also match a word merely ENDING in mix (`premix `), which is
fail-closed and acceptable but should be a deliberate choice, not an accident.

On the verifier: its falsifiability step did not discriminate, and that is a verifier
miss worth recording even though routing is to the implementer. All seven mutants
(a,b1,b2,c,d,e,f) were shape-preserving — each was written in the detector's own
vocabulary. Mutant (e) attacks the same clause as BLOCKER 2 but inserted a line-anchored
`mix run -e '...'`, i.e. the one form the regex catches; no mutant used
`MIX_ENV=… mix`, `cd x && mix`, or `elixir -S mix`, and no mutant checked out PR code
without `uses:`. Mutation testing that only mutates inside the assertion's own syntax
class cannot find an aperture defect. The verifier also enumerated all 38 musts and
passed while the ONE requirement this ticket advances had two false greens, so the
enumeration bought breadth, not depth. Credit where due: verifier advisory notes 1-3
(unguarded artifact-handoff phrase, exact-equality strictness, dead assertions at :99-101)
were all accurate and note 3 independently corroborates the critic.

Bounce reason: The guard must actually enforce both verbs of the operative clause
("shall not check out or execute pull-request-provided code"). Treat the critic's
snippets as requirements to satisfy, not code to paste unexamined.

1. BLOCKER — checkout aperture. Stop keying the checkout clause off `uses:` alone. The
   deploy job must be rejected if PR code enters by ANY route: (a) keep the existing
   exact `with.ref == "${{ github.base_ref }}"` pin on every `actions/checkout` step;
   (b) additionally scan every deploy `run:` string and reject PR-ref acquisition
   (`pull/<N>/head|merge` refspecs and any `github.event.pull_request.head` fragment);
   (c) allowlist deploy's `uses:` set rather than filtering it, so a NEW action cannot
   smuggle a checkout past a filter that only knows one action name. Today's legitimate
   set is `actions/checkout@v4` and `actions/download-artifact@v4` (template :126, :131).

2. BLOCKER — execution aperture. `invokes_mix?/1` must not be line-anchored. At minimum
   it must catch the forms the critic measured: `MIX_ENV=prod mix run …`,
   `cd apps/x && mix release`, `./bin/mix …`, `OUT=$(mix …)`, `bash -c 'mix …'`,
   `elixir -S mix …`. Handle the `` `mix spec.review` `` prose collision at template :184
   by excluding backtick spans (see the odd-backtick hazard above), not by re-anchoring.
   Keep the :113 render canary — it is what makes the deploy assertion non-vacuous, and
   it must still be green after the change.

3. SHOULD FIX — vacuous render assertion. `render["permissions"] || %{}` (:61) makes the
   comprehension and both refutes no-ops when render declares no `permissions:` block at
   all; deleting that block leaves the test green. Assert symmetrically with deploy:
   `assert render["permissions"] == %{"contents" => "read"}`. Also guard the
   `permissions: write-all` shorthand, which is a binary and currently raises
   Protocol.UndefinedError out of the comprehension instead of failing an assertion.

4. SHOULD FIX — remove the dead assertions at :35-41 and :99-102. Both sit behind an
   exact-equality `==` that already subsumes them. In a security guard, unreachable
   checks that read as independent coverage are actively misleading. Consider splitting
   the :72 test so a failure names its clause (permissions / checkout pin / no-execute)
   without reading the message body.

5. Re-falsify with DISAGREEING shapes, not restatements of the assertion. The commit
   record must show RED for, at minimum: a `run:`-tier PR-head checkout in deploy, and
   an evasive mix form (e.g. `MIX_ENV=prod mix run ./rendered/hook.exs`) in a deploy
   step — the two mutations that are green today. Re-confirm the unmutated template is
   GREEN, including render's 3 mix hits.
